title: Capacity handoff protocol and autoscale policy runbook
creator: Evelyn Chen
description: Create an authoritative runbook and decision protocol for converting an approved capacity reservation into a production-dedicated fleet with clear autoscale policy defaults and SLA-bound throughput guarantees. This ticket covers the end-to-end handoff: intake validation, entitlement scoring, approval lanes, policy templating for autoscaling and burst, canary/probation window, chargeback tagging, and capacity planning signals used by finance and SRE. The goal is a repeatable, auditable flow that reduces onboarding time from weeks to days while preserving predictable SLOs and cost forecasting.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form fields and validation rules defined and added to the capacity portal UI spec
Three autoscale policy templates (low-latency, cost-optimized, balanced) documented with parameter defaults and trade-offs
Approval matrix mapping entitlement score -> approval lane implemented and tested in sandbox
Handoff checklist covering network/VPC, KMS policy, billing tags, model pinning, and runbook steps published to Confluence
Simulation run shows <5% SLA violation risk for canonical workload profiles when using recommended autoscale template
Telemetry hooks and dashboard for probation window live and linked in the onboarding playbook
decisions: Use entitlement scoring (usage history + business criticality + security tier) to pick approval lane rather than manual triage
Autoscale policies will provide three opinionated presets; customers can opt into custom policies but will incur an SRE review for custom autoscale parameters
Throughput guarantees will be expressed as committed RPS and median p99 latency targets and backed by reserved GPU pool sizing with a 10% buffer for burst
Canary/probation window will be 72 hours by default with automated rollback to hosted variants on sustained error rate >1.5%
